Frequently asked questions

Caresse vs Dipsea — your questions.

children.html: What Dipsea alternative offers audio in Spanish or French?

Caresse generates audio sessions in French, English, Spanish and Portuguese. The Portuguese interface is available on Android; the iOS update is awaiting approval. Free demos are in French, English and Spanish. Listen to demos free in the app, then use credits to create a session around your names and preferences, without a subscription.
Are all personalized Caresse sessions free?
No. Downloading the app and listening to demos are free. Generating personalized sessions uses paid credits. Caresse does not require a subscription; prices are shown in the app before purchase.
Can I buy sessions in anonymous mode?

Yes. Anonymous mode lets you use Caresse and buy sessions without creating a Caresse account. Purchases go through the App Store or Google Play and require an Apple or Google account on the store you use, with its payment method. Anonymous mode applies to your use of Caresse, not to the transaction with the store.
Is Dipsea free, and what does the subscription include?

Dipsea offers limited previews and a 7-day trial with its annual plan, while full catalog access requires a subscription: $69.99 per year or $12.99 per month, as listed on 10 November 2026. Store prices and promotions change over time, so treat this as a snapshot rather than a quote. Caresse takes a different approach: audio demos play free in the app, with no account and no trial to start.
What is a free alternative to Dipsea?

Caresse offers browser-playable audio demos without an account, email or payment. It is not a free unlimited catalog: personalized sessions are purchased individually. The difference is that you can hear the actual audio experience before deciding, without beginning a subscription.
Can I listen to Caresse before paying, without creating an account?

Yes. Caresse offers pre-generated audio demos in English, French and Spanish, playable immediately — no sign-up, no email, no account. You hear the sound quality, the voice, the atmosphere and the intensity levels before any decision. Demos don't use your name or profile, but they faithfully reflect the experience.
Does Caresse require an account like Dipsea?

No. Anonymous mode lets you use the app without creating a Caresse account. Purchases go through the App Store or Google Play and require an Apple or Google account on the store you use. That's a structural difference from Dipsea, where signing up is a prerequisite to access the catalog.
What's the main difference between Caresse and Dipsea?

Dipsea is a US library of erotic audio stories: a large catalog of pre-recorded stories in English, subscription-based, built for passive listening, solo or as a couple. Caresse generates a unique scenario every session: your names are spoken aloud, duration varies with generation, intensity, practices and atmosphere are configured by you. It's a guided, personalized experience, not a library of fiction to browse.
Does Caresse run on a subscription or pay-per-session?

Caresse is pay-per-session — no mandatory monthly subscription. You pay when you want a new experience, you don't pay for months you don't use it. Dipsea runs on a subscription: a 7-day free trial, then $69.99/year (or $12.99/month), regardless of how often you listen.
Does Caresse offer as large a catalog as Dipsea?

Not in the same sense. Dipsea has a large catalog of stories written by authors, fixed and updated regularly. Caresse doesn't offer a catalog to browse: every session is generated on demand from your intimate profile, with an essentially infinite combination of genders, names, practices, accessories, intensity and atmosphere. You never replay the same thing, and you're not waiting on a release calendar.
Does Dipsea work in languages other than English?

To our knowledge, Dipsea is English-only, with no French or Spanish version available. Caresse generates audio sessions in French, English, Spanish and Portuguese. The Portuguese interface is available on Android; the iOS update is awaiting approval. Free demos are in French, English and Spanish.
Dipsea or Caresse: which one for a shared couple experience?

Dipsea is built primarily for individual fiction listening, even if some stories work for a couple. Caresse has a native duo mode: both partners' names are woven into the scenario, and the experience is designed as a shared, guided moment — not the reading of a third-party story.
